mainTopic: טומאת אהל of non-Jews, a כהן גדול marrying a widow or יבמה, and a כהן marrying an אילונית
overview: The amud opens with the ruling of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי that graves of גוים do not spread טומאת אהל, because only Jews are called 'אדם'. The גמרא tests this with three פסוקים. Two of them call non-Jews 'אדם' only to set people apart from animals. The third is about the war with מדין, and it leads to a back-and-forth with the רבנן. רבינא then explains that non-Jewish bodies still make people טמא by touching and carrying. Next, a משנה rules that a כהן who betrothed a widow and then became כהן גדול may marry her, but he may not marry a יבמה. The גמרא learns this from 'יקח אשה' and tells how יהושע בן גמלא was made כהן גדול through a bribe. Another משנה says a כהן גדול does חליצה, not יבום, and the גמרא explains this with a rabbinic גזירה. The last משנה is about a כהן marrying an אילונית, and the גמרא begins to ask why the משנה speaks only about a כהן.

steps.title: Graves of non-Jews do not make things impure through a tent
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי rules that graves of גוים do not spread טומאת אהל. He learns it from יחזקאל 34:31, where only the Jewish people are called 'אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Graves of non-Jews do not make things impure through a tent. The פסוק says: 'And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are אדם.' You are called אדם, and the non-Jews are not called אדם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: a non-Jew's grave does not make people or things under the same roof טמא. It gives a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of טומאת אהל is written as 'אדם כי ימות באהל', meaning 'when an אדם dies in a tent'. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי argues that the word 'אדם' in the Torah's legal sense means a Jew. He shows this from יחזקאל, which says 'you are אדם'. So the special rule of tent-impurity applies only to a Jewish body.

keyTerms.meaning: through a tent or roof, meaning by being under the same covering as the body

steps.confusionAlert: This is only about טומאת אהל, impurity spread by being under one roof. The rule does not say non-Jewish bodies carry no טומאה at all. It only takes away this one way that טומאה spreads.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole סוגיא that follows tests one idea: does 'אדם' in a פסוק always mean only Jews?

phrases.english: The graves of non-Jews do not make things impure through a tent,
phrases.notes: This is the ruling of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, the one the rest of the piece goes back and forth about.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And you, My sheep,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 34:31

phrases.english: 'the sheep of My pasture, are men (אדם).'
You are called 'אדם',
and the non-Jews are not called 'אדם'.
phrases.notes: The tent-impurity law is written about 'אדם' (במדבר 19:14), so it applies only to whoever is called אדם.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִבְרֵי גוֹיִם אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the sugya by giving the ruling of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי and its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Graves of גוים do not spread טומאת אהל, because only Jews are called 'אדם'.

steps.title: Challenge from the captives of מדין, called 'נפש אדם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling with במדבר 31:40, where the Midianite captives are called 'נפש אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: the פסוק says 'And the persons (נפש אדם) were sixteen thousand'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 1. Here is a פסוק where non-Jews are called 'אדם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea in step 1 was that non-Jews are never called 'אדם'. The captives from מדין were not Jews, yet the Torah calls them 'נפש אדם'. That seems to break the proof.

phrases.english: They challenged: 'And the persons (נפש אדם) were sixteen thousand'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:40. These were the captives taken from מדין, who were not Jewish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that non-Jews are not called 'אדם'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק calls non-Jewish captives 'נפש אדם', so non-Jews can be called אדם.

steps.title: Answer: the word 'אדם' there sets people apart from animals
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אדם' is used there only to separate the human captives from the animals listed in the same section.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of the animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In that פסוק, 'אדם' is only a way to say 'humans, not animals'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section about the spoils of מדין counts animals and people together. The Torah says 'אדם' only so we know which count is the people. That is a plain description, not the legal title 'אדם' used for טומאת אהל.

phrases.english: Because of the animals.
phrases.notes: He means the Torah needed a word to tell the people apart from the sheep and cattle counted right next to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the meaning of the word in that context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אדם' in the Midian פסוק is the same title as in the טומאה law.

steps.title: Challenge from the people of נינוה, called 'אדם'
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge comes from יונה 4:11, where the people of נינוה, who were not Jews, are called 'אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says about נינוה: 'In which there are more than one hundred twenty thousand אדם who do not know their right hand from their left (and many animals)'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק where non-Jews are called 'אדם'. It challenges the rule again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נינוה was a city of non-Jews, yet the נביא calls its people 'אדם'. This is a second case that seems to go against the idea from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: his right hand from his left

phrases.english: 'In which there are more'
phrases.notes: יונה 4:11, about the city of נינוה.

phrases.english: 'than twelve times ten thousand people (אדם)'

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדַע בֵּין יְמִינוֹ לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ
phrases.english: 'who do not know their right hand from their left'
'(and many animals)'!
phrases.notes: These words finish the פסוק. Some versions print them and some don't. They matter, because the answer points to these animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲשֶׁר יֶשׁ בָּהּ הַרְבֵּה מִשְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה רִבּוֹא אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that non-Jews are not called 'אדם'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The non-Jewish people of נינוה are called 'אדם'.

steps.title: Same answer: the people of נינוה are set apart from the animals
steps.stepSummary: Here too, 'אדם' is used only to separate the people from the animals mentioned in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of the animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. The פסוק mentions animals, so 'אדם' just means 'humans'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק says 'and many animals'. Because animals are listed too, the word 'אדם' only tells us which group is human. So again, it is not the legal title.

phrases.english: Because of the animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 the same way step 3 answered step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the meaning of the word in that context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אדם' about נינוה is the legal title.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only separates people from the animals in the same פסוק.

steps.title: Challenge: soldiers had to purify themselves after the war with מדין
steps.stepSummary: במדבר 31:19 tells the soldiers who killed or touched the dead in the war with מדין to purify themselves. This suggests that non-Jewish bodies make people טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Whoever killed a person and whoever touched a slain body, purify yourselves'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge. This one is not about the word 'אדם' but about actual טומאה from non-Jewish dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soldiers fought non-Jews, yet they needed purification. That seems to show that the bodies of non-Jews give off טומאה. The 'because of the animals' answer cannot help here.
steps.confusionAlert: Touching a body and being under one roof with it are different ways of becoming טמא. The challenge assumes this purification covered tent-impurity too, so it is aimed at רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's rule.

phrases.english: 'Whoever killed a person'
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:19, said to the soldiers returning from the war with מדין.

phrases.english: 'and whoever touched a slain body, purify yourselves'!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הוֹרֵג נֶפֶשׁ וְכֹל נוֹגֵעַ בֶּחָלָל תִּתְחַטְּאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different kind of challenge against step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that non-Jewish bodies do not spread טומאת אהל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Soldiers who fought non-Jews needed purification, so non-Jewish dead must make people טמא.

steps.title: Answer: maybe one Jewish soldier was killed
steps.stepSummary: The purification may have been needed because of a Jewish soldier who died in the battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps one Jew was killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. The טומאה could have come from a Jewish body, not from the Midianites.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even one Jewish soldier fell, his body could make the others טמא through an אהל. Then the command to purify proves nothing about non-Jewish bodies.

phrases.english: Perhaps one Jew was killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers a different cause for the טומאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The purification was because of the Midianite dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: It may have been because of a Jewish casualty.

steps.title: The רבנן reply: no Jewish soldier was missing
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject the answer with במדבר 31:49: 'not one man of us is missing'. So no Jew died in the war.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: 'Not one man of us is missing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back on the answer of step 7. The Torah itself says that no Jewish soldier was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no Jew died, the only bodies around were Midianite ones. So the purification must have been because of them. That brings back the challenge against רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages, who disagree with רבי שמעון בן יוחאי

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: 'Not one man of us is missing.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:49. The army officers said this when they counted the soldiers after the battle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that a Jewish soldier died.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A פסוק says no soldier was missing.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: 'not missing' means no one sinned
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי reads 'not one man of us is missing' as being about sin, not about death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: 'Not one man of us is missing' means missing through sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers the רבנן. The פסוק means no soldier was 'missing' in his behavior, meaning no one sinned. It does not mean no one died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the פסוק is read as being about sin, it no longer proves that every soldier survived. So it is still possible that a Jew was killed and caused the טומאה. His rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי holds that only Jewish bodies spread טומאת אהל, since only Jews are called 'אדם'. The פסוקים that call non-Jews 'אדם' do so only to set them apart from animals. The purification after the war with מדין can be explained by a Jewish soldier who died, if 'not missing' means 'not sinning'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
'Not one man of us is missing' means through sin.
phrases.notes: He means no one was 'lacking' in his deeds. It doesn't tell us that nobody died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: ״לֹא נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ״ — לַעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 8 and brings back the answer of step 7.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not missing' means no soldier sinned, so a Jew may have died.

steps.title: רבינא: touching and carrying still cause impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers the challenge from the war with מדין another way. The פסוק only left non-Jews out of טומאת אהל, not out of טומאה through touching or carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Fine, the verse left them out of making things impure through a tent, since it says 'a man (אדם) who dies in a tent.' But did the verse leave them out of making things impure through touching and carrying?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a simpler answer to the question from the war with מדין (Step 6). The soldiers needed purification because they touched and carried bodies, and non-Jewish bodies can cause that kind of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אדם' is used only in the פסוק about a tent, so it only takes non-Jews out of טומאת אהל. Touching and carrying are a different kind of טומאה, and no פסוק takes non-Jews out of those. So רבי שמעון בן יוחאי has no problem, and there is no need for the 'Jewish soldier died' answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that / even if we accept that
From making things impure through a tent (being under one roof)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, non-Jewish bodies do not cause טומאת אהל, but they do cause טומאה through touching and carrying.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying non-Jewish bodies cause טומאה in every way. He agrees they do not cause טומאת אהל. He only says touching and carrying are different.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Granted that the verse excluded them
from making things impure in a tent,
as it is written: "A man, when he dies in a tent,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:14

phrases.english: but from touching and carrying
did the verse exclude them?
phrases.notes: He means: of course not. No פסוק leaves them out of these kinds of טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the challenge in Step 6, so the answer in Steps 7-9 is not needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the exclusion (only tent-impurity)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Purification after the war with מדין shows that non-Jewish bodies cause טומאה in every way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The purification was needed because of touching and carrying, which non-Jewish bodies do cause, even according to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each type of טומאה can have its own rules, so a limit on one type does not carry over to the others.

steps.title: משנה: betrothed widow may be married after appointment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a כהן who betrothed a widow and was then appointed כהן גדול may complete the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a כהן betrothed an אלמנה and was then appointed to be כהן גדול, he may marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Normally a כהן גדול may not marry a widow, but here the אירוסין happened before he became כהן גדול, so he may finish the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is timing. At the time of אירוסין he was an ordinary כהן, who may marry a widow. The משנה rules that being appointed afterward does not stop him from doing the נישואין.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothed (did the first stage of marriage, אירוסין)
High Priest, who may not marry a widow
He may marry her (complete the marriage)

phrases.english: MISHNAH: If he betrothed a widow
and was appointed to be High Priest,
he may marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who betrothed a widow before becoming כהן גדול may complete the marriage after his appointment.

steps.title: The story of יהושע בן גמלא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה supports its ruling with a real event: יהושע בן גמלא betrothed מרתא בת ביתוס, was appointed כהן גדול by the king, and then married her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was an incident with יהושע בן גמלא, who betrothed מרתא בת ביתוס. The king appointed him כהן גדול, and he married her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its ruling with a story of a כהן גדול who actually did this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרתא בת ביתוס was a widow. יהושע בן גמלא betrothed her before his appointment and married her after it. This matches the rule just stated. Notice the wording 'the king appointed him', because the גמרא will focus on it later.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Yehoshua ben Gamla,
who betrothed Marta bat Baitos,
and the king appointed him to be High Priest,
and he married her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of Step 11 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a כהן גדול may marry a widow he betrothed before his appointment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What actually happened with יהושע בן גמלא and מרתא בת ביתוס.

steps.title: משנה: a waiting יבמה may not be married
steps.stepSummary: If a woman waiting for יבום fell to an ordinary כהן who was then appointed כהן גדול, he may not marry her, even if he already did מאמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow waiting for her יבם who fell to a כהן הדיוט, and he was then appointed כהן גדול: even if he already did מאמר with her, he may not marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite ruling for a יבמה. Even after a מאמר, a כהן גדול may not marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think מאמר works like אירוסין, so she should be like the widow in Step 11. The משנה says no. She is still a widow, and he may not marry her once he is כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה
Became bound to him for יבום
A rabbinic form of betrothal that a יבם does with a יבמה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume מאמר is the same as regular אירוסין. The משנה treats the יבמה differently from the widow in Step 11.

phrases.english: A woman waiting for her yavam who fell
before an ordinary priest,
phrases.notes: He was her late husband's brother, so she was waiting for him to do יבום.

phrases.english: and he was appointed to be High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָשָׂה בָּהּ מַאֲמָר
phrases.english: even though he had performed levirate betrothal with her,
he may not marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁנָּפְלָה לִפְנֵי כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a contrasting case: unlike a betrothed widow, a יבמה may not be married.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול may not marry his יבמה, even if he did מאמר with her before his appointment.

steps.title: Source: 'He shall take a wife'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'יקח אשה' that a כהן גדול may marry a widow he betrothed before his appointment.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: How do we know that if he betrothed an אלמנה and was then appointed כהן גדול, he may marry her? The פסוק says: 'יקח אשה', 'He shall take a wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's first ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about whom a כהן גדול may marry adds the words 'יקח אשה'. The ברייתא reads these words as including this case: a woman who was already 'his wife' through אירוסין may be fully married to him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall take a wife', the words used for the source

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that if he betrothed a widow
and was appointed to be High Priest, that he may marry her?
The verse teaches: "He shall take a wife."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from the תורה for the משנה's first ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'יקח אשה' allow a כהן גדול to marry a widow he betrothed before his appointment.

steps.title: Then a yevamah should be allowed too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the extra words include a betrothed widow, they should also include a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a widow waiting for her יבם should also be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source. If 'יקח אשה' includes the widow, why not the יבמה as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both women are widows, and both were connected to him before he became כהן גדול. So if the פסוק includes one, it seems it should include the other, which goes against the משנה.

phrases.english: If so,
a woman waiting for her yavam too should be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source in Step 14 using the ruling in Step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the extra words include anyone already bound to him, they should include the יבמה too, but the משנה forbids her.

steps.title: 'A wife', not a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אשה' means his own wife, and that leaves out a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A wife', and not a יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'wife' itself limits the rule to a woman who is his own wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The betrothed widow became his own wife through his own אירוסין. A יבמה came to him because she was his brother's wife, so she is not called 'his wife' in the same way. The extra words therefore include the first woman but not the second.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother's widow who is bound to the brother for יבום

steps.whatToRemember: 'יקח אשה' lets a כהן גדול marry a widow he betrothed earlier, but the word 'אשה' leaves out a יבמה.

phrases.english: "A wife," and not a yevamah.
phrases.notes: She was his brother's wife, not his own wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words include the יבמה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אשה' means a woman who became his own wife, and that leaves out a יבמה.

steps.title: Close reading: 'appointed him', not 'was appointed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the משנה says the king 'appointed him' (מנהו) and not that he 'was appointed' (נתמנה).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'An incident with יהושע, etc.' It says 'appointed him', yes. It does not say 'was appointed'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story in the משנה and notices a change in the wording. This sets up רב יוסף's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everywhere else the משנה says 'נתמנה', meaning he was appointed in the proper way. In the story it says 'מנהו המלך', meaning the king put him in. The change hints that this appointment was not done properly.

phrases.english: "An incident with Yehoshua, etc."
"Appointed him": yes,
"was appointed": no.
phrases.notes: The king put him in. He was not chosen the proper way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story in Step 12 and reads its wording closely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wording 'מנהו' shows the appointment came from the king, not through the proper process.

steps.title: רב יוסף sees a conspiracy
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains the wording: there was something improper behind this appointment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I see a conspiracy here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains what the unusual wording is hinting at. The appointment was a scheme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף ties the wording 'מנהו' to a hidden deal. The next step gives the proof for his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'tied up'; here, a plot or conspiracy

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I see a conspiracy here.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'I see something tied up here', meaning a hidden deal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: קְטִיר קָחָזֵינָא הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the wording in Step 17 is hinting at.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע בן גמלא's appointment came from an improper scheme.

steps.title: רב אסי: the bribe to King ינאי
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי reports that מרתא בת ביתוס gave King ינאי a large container of dinars until he made יהושע בן גמלא a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אסי said: מרתא בת ביתוס brought a תרקבא full of dinars to King ינאי until he appointed יהושע בן גמלא as one of the כהנים גדולים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף's claim is backed up by רב אסי's report of the bribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the משנה says 'the king appointed him'. מרתא paid for the appointment. The ruling of the משנה still stands, because he did marry her after he became כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A large measure, half a סאה

steps.whatToRemember: The story's wording 'the king appointed him' hints that יהושע בן גמלא got the position through a bribe, not the proper way. The משנה still uses his case to show that he may marry a widow he betrothed earlier.

phrases.english: As Rav Asi said:
A tarkav full of dinars

phrases.aramaic: עַיִּילָהּ לֵיהּ מָרְתָּא בַּת בַּיְתּוֹס לְיַנַּאי מַלְכָּא
phrases.english: Marta bat Baitos brought to King Yannai

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּמוֹקֵי לֵיהּ לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן גַּמְלָא
phrases.english: until he appointed Yehoshua ben Gamla
among the High Priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the evidence for רב יוסף's claim in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that there was a conspiracy behind the appointment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי's report that מרתא בת ביתוס bribed King ינאי.

steps.title: A כהן גדול whose brother died does חליצה, not יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a כהן גדול whose brother died childless does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול whose brother died performs חליצה and does not perform יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It says that if a כהן גדול's brother dies without children, the כהן גדול releases the widow with חליצה instead of marrying her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may not marry an אלמנה, and his brother's widow is an אלמנה. So instead of יבום, the only option the משנה gives is חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Performs חליצה, the ceremony that releases the widow
Performs יבום, marrying the brother's widow

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A High Priest whose brother died
phrases.notes: He means the brother died without children, which is when יבום or חליצה comes up.

phrases.english: performs chalitza and does not perform levirate marriage

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story of יהושע בן גמלא's appointment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול does חליצה, not יבום, for his brother's widow.

steps.title: The משנה's rule covers both betrothal and marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה makes no exception. It applies whether the brother had only done ארוסין or had full נשואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches this with no exceptions. It makes no difference if she was widowed after betrothal or after marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה's rule has no exceptions. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying the rule is the same for ארוסין and נשואין, the גמרא includes a widow who is still a virgin. That case will be harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches the rule with no exceptions
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: GEMARA: It teaches categorically
it is no different if she is a widow from betrothal
and it is no different if she is a widow from marriage

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the scope of the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule covers a widow from ארוסין and from נשואין alike.

steps.title: Why doesn't yibum override the ban for a betrothed widow?
steps.stepSummary: For a widow from נשואין, יבום would break both an עשה and a לא תעשה, so it cannot override them. A widow from ארוסין is still a virgin, so only a לא תעשה stands in the way, and the עשה of יבום should override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a widow from marriage, because marrying her would break a positive command and a prohibition, and a positive command does not push aside a prohibition together with a positive command. But for a widow from betrothal, the positive command of יבום should come and push aside the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's broad rule. In the betrothal case, יבום should be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that an עשה can override a plain לא תעשה. It cannot override a לא תעשה joined with an עשה. A betrothed widow is still a virgin, so the עשה to marry a virgin is not broken, and only the לא תעשה against an אלמנה is left.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the positive command come and push aside

steps.confusionAlert: The עשה here for a widow from נשואין is the כהן גדול's מצוה to marry a virgin. It is not the מצוה of יבום, which is the עשה trying to override.

phrases.english: Granted, from marriage
it is a positive command and a prohibition
phrases.notes: After marriage she is no longer a virgin, so marrying her breaks the מצוה to marry a virgin and the ban on widows.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
phrases.english: and a positive command does not override a prohibition and a positive command together
But from betrothal

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא עֲשֵׂה וְיִדְחֶה אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.english: let the positive command come and override the prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad scope noted in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule as it applies to a widow from ארוסין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a plain לא תעשה blocks יבום here, and an עשה normally overrides a plain לא תעשה.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree: first intercourse forbidden because of the second
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law יבום would be allowed. The רבנן forbade even the first act because of later acts, which would break the prohibition without any מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a rabbinic decree. The first act of intercourse is forbidden because of the second act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ban on יבום for a betrothed widow is a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first act fulfills the מצוה of יבום. Every later act would break the לא תעשה with no מצוה to override it. So the רבנן forbade the first act too, and that is why the משנה's rule has no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול never does יבום. For a widow from נשואין the Torah forbids it, and for a widow from ארוסין the רבנן forbid it with a גזירה about the second act.

phrases.english: It is a decree on the first act of intercourse
phrases.notes: Only the first act counts as the מצוה of יבום; later acts are just marriage, with no מצוה.

phrases.english: due to the second act of intercourse

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה בִּיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה אַטּוּ בִּיאָה שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עשה of יבום should override the plain לא תעשה for a betrothed widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law it could, but the רבנן forbade the first act because of the second act.

steps.title: A כהן הדיוט may not marry an אילונית unless he has a wife and children
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says a כהן הדיוט may not marry an אילונית, a woman who cannot have children, unless he already has a wife and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: A regular כהן may not marry an אילונית, unless he has a wife and children.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a regular כהן marrying a woman who cannot have children. This is the first view, and a dispute follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view allows it if he already has a wife and children. The משנה does not give a reason here, but that condition will be challenged by רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular kohen, not the High Priest
A woman who is physically undeveloped and cannot have children

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט לֹא יִשָּׂא אַיְלוֹנִית
phrases.english: MISHNAH: A common priest may not marry an aylonit

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה וּבָנִים
phrases.english: unless he has a wife and children

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט לֹא יִשָּׂא אַיְלוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן הדיוט may marry an אילונית only if he already has a wife and children.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: an אילונית is the זונה of the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids a כהן to marry an אילונית even if he has a wife and children, because she is the זונה the Torah forbids to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even if he has a wife and children, he may not marry an אילונית, because she is the זונה mentioned in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first view and forbids an אילונית to a כהן in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה the problem is not only about having children. He puts the אילונית in the Torah's category of זונה, which is forbidden to every כהן, so having a wife and children does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forbidden to a kohen by the Torah

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה וּבָנִים
phrases.english: Even if he has a wife and children
he may not marry an aylonit
because she is the zona stated in the Torah
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first view in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אילונית is a זונה and is forbidden to any כהן.

steps.title: The חכמים: only a גיורת, a משוחררת, or one who had forbidden relations is a זונה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים limit זונה to a גיורת, a משוחררת, and a woman who had forbidden relations. An אילונית is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: A זונה is only a female convert, a freed maidservant, and a woman who had licentious relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה by listing who is a זונה. An אילונית is not on their list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים give a closed list for זונה. Because an אילונית is not on it, she is not forbidden as a זונה, against רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. The first view lets a כהן marry an אילונית if he has a wife and children. רבי יהודה calls her a זונה and forbids her always. The חכמים limit זונה to a convert, a freed maidservant, or a woman who had forbidden relations.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say
A zona is only a female convert
and a freed maidservant
and one who had licentious intercourse
phrases.notes: He means relations with a man she was forbidden to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's definition of זונה from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a גיורת, a משוחררת, or a woman who had forbidden relations is a זונה; an אילונית is not.

steps.title: Why does the משנה single out a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא asks רב הונא: the reason for not marrying an אילונית is פריה ורביה, but every Jew has that מצוה, not only כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The ריש גלותא said to רב הונא: What is the reason? It is because of the מצוה to have children. Is it only כהנים who are commanded to have children, and ישראלים are not commanded?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ריש גלותא asks why the משנה says only a כהן may not marry an אילונית. The reason seems to be פריה ורביה, and that מצוה applies to every Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 24) said a כהן הדיוט may not marry an אילונית unless he already has a wife and children. That last condition shows the concern is having children, not כהונה. So the ריש גלותא asks: why does the משנה say 'כהן' at all?

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in בבל
The מצוה to be fruitful and multiply, meaning to have children

steps.confusionAlert: The ריש גלותא does not doubt that a ישראל must have children. He is asking why the משנה wrote 'כהן' when the rule seems to apply to everyone.

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: The Exilarch said to Rav Huna:
What is the reason?
It is because of being fruitful and multiplying.
phrases.notes: This is the reason a כהן can't marry an אילונית unless he already has children, the rule from our משנה.

phrases.english: Is it priests who are commanded to be fruitful and multiply
and Israelites are not commanded?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב הוּנָא: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה given in steps 24 to 26 and questions why the first clause is worded about a כהן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'כהן הדיוט' in the first clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's condition (he has a wife and children) shows the reason is פריה ורביה. That מצוה is shared by all Jews, so naming a כהן seems pointless or misleading.

steps.title: The first clause says כהן to match the last clause
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the rule applies to everyone. The משנה said כהן only because it wanted to teach the last clause, where רבי יהודה speaks about a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because the תנא wants to teach the latter clause: רבי יהודה says: Even if he has a wife...
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains why the משנה used the word כהן. It wanted the first part to match the last part, where רבי יהודה rules about a כהן even if he has a wife. His answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's ruling (step 25) really is about כהנים only, because he calls an אילונית a זונה, which is forbidden only to a כהן. To keep the two parts of the משנה parallel, the first part also says כהן. The first part's law, though, applies to every Jew because of פריה ורביה.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
To teach, meaning to state it in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a משנה may word its first part to match its later part. The first part's wording does not always limit its law.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא answering the ריש גלותא.

phrases.english: Because he wants to teach the latter clause:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of our משנה. The 'latter clause' is רבי יהודה's ruling from step 25.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה
phrases.english: Even if he has a wife
phrases.notes: The quote keeps going on the next amud: 'and children, he may not marry her, because she is a זונה.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ריש גלותא's question from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the רישא is worded to match the סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'כהן' in the first clause suggests the law applies only to כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause applies to all Jews because of פריה ורביה. 'כהן' appears only to match רבי יהודה's סיפא, which really is limited to כהנים because of the זונה prohibition.
